subject.title: Feature: configPatch in plugin manifest — automatic config setup on install

question: What path-scoped, consented authority should third-party plugin manifests have to change persisted OpenClaw configuration during installation?
rationale: Implementation cannot safely proceed until maintainers decide which paths plugins may own, whether approval is mandatory, and how conflicts, arrays, upgrades, user overrides, and recovery behave.

options.title: Consented setup intents
options.body: Allow validated, path-scoped intents only after showing the exact diff and recording provenance for repair or removal guidance.

options.title: Automatic manifest merge
options.body: Apply manifest patches without confirmation and accept the broader package-trust, overwrite, and upgrade risks.

options.title: Separate setup flow
options.body: Keep installation plugin-scoped and require explicit onboarding or configure flows for all additional configuration.

recommendation.title: Consented setup intents
recommendation.body: Allow validated, path-scoped intents only after showing the exact diff and recording provenance for repair or removal guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: This person supplied the existing contract review and has the strongest history signal across the central manifest and installation paths.
